rationale: Judges 19 retells the shape of Genesis 19:1-11 in Israel's own territory: a traveler in the city square at evening, a resident who takes him in and says 'do not spend the night in the square' (Judges 19:20; compare Genesis 19:2), men of the city who surround the house demanding the guest 'so we can have relations with him' (19:22; Genesis 19:5 reads 'so we can have relations with them'), a host who answers 'my brothers' and calls it a 'wicked thing' (19:23; Genesis 19:7), and an offer of a virgin daughter (19:24; Genesis 19:8). The Cambridge Bible states that 'beset the house ... know him' are 'The same words in Genesis 19:4-5' and that 'It looks as if the present narrative had been deliberately conformed here and there to the description of the immorality of the Sodomites,' adding that in Judges 19:24 'the phrases are identical with those in Genesis 19:8'; Keil and Delitzsch call the demand 'the very same demand that the Sodomites had made of Lot.' Graded parallel, not explicit_reference, because Judges never names Sodom; graded strong because the shared sequence and wording are checkable and named commentators draw the link. Unlike Genesis 19, where the angels intervene, Judges 19:25 narrates the rape and abuse of the Levite's concubine.
